packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-17 -- unverified image reading (first reader)
No identification of the work was revealed in my context. I did nothing beyond the rules.

LAYOUT SURVEY (from overview image-001)
- image-001: reduced overview of face A. A horizontal parchment strip (approx. 19.5 cm wide x 6 cm high by the scale), clearly cut from a larger leaf; top and bottom edges ragged, bottom edge with losses. A grey rectangle (masking label/patch) covers the left end, middle height.
- Text in two columns (left column ~ left half, right column ~ right half, intercolumnium around the middle where a large brown stain lies). About 16-17 lines visible per column; lines at top and bottom are cut.
- Small Gothic book hand, densely abbreviated, brown ink. Red paragraph marks / red-touched initials (pilcrows) at several line starts in both columns; a larger red initial or sign near the top in the middle region (around x~960). Red underline-like strokes near the top of the left column.
- A modern pencil note written vertically in the right margin (reads something like "...Stams...").
- Tentative: scholastic prose with paragraph divisions; no gloss apparatus visible at this scale.
- Tiles image-002 and image-003 presumably cover the left and right halves of this face at native resolution.

TILE image-002 (native tile, left part of face A: left column, plus left edge of right column at far right)
Viewed with my crops rscratch/packet-17/002a.jpg (upper, autocontrast, 1.6x) and 002b.jpg (lower).
Observations: the left column has ~17 lines; the hand is a small, very compressed Gothic textualis with heavy abbreviation and many single letters set off by points (e.g. ".a." ".b." ".c." ".g."), which look like letter-sigla (lettered terms/points in an argument) rather than words. Red-touched paragraph initials at lines 3, 4 (mid-line), 5 (end), 9 (mid-line), 11 and 16. At right edge (x~1440-1560) a large red initial (looks like a "Q" or "D"?) with a red vertical stroke down the intercolumnium and red paragraph sign above it: this belongs to the right column. Surface is badly abraded; lower half (lines 10-16) is mostly faded to ghosts.
Line numbers count from top of image-002. Readings are very uncertain; abbreviations marked with ' or ~ where I could not resolve them.

002 L16 [red ¶] [illegible] ... ... (bottom, partly cut)
Honest assessment: I could not secure a single continuous phrase in this column. Only isolated tokens; the letter-sigla pattern (a, b, c, d, g separated by points) is the most reliable observation.

TILE image-003 (native tile, right part of face A: right column; at far left the line-ends of the left column, overlapping image-002's right edge)
Viewed with crops rscratch/packet-17/003a.jpg and 003b.jpg (grey, autocontrast, 1.6x).
Overlap: x 0-200 of image-003 repeats the line-ends of the left column already seen at the right edge of image-002 (e.g. "...ē fi", "...ꝯ ... s", "...a . g", "...ꝗ . c", "...ꝯ . r"); not new text.
Observations: right column ~16-17 lines. In the intercolumnium/left of the right column a large red initial (S-shaped, possibly "S" or "Q") with a red stroke running down the margin, with a red paragraph sign above it at line 3; a red paragraph sign at line 2 near the right end of the column (x~1180) followed by a word. A heavy brown stain covers the upper middle of the right column (lines 1-9). Modern pencil, written vertically in right margin: "Stams, StA, Fg. 145 ..." (shelf/fragment note; the last characters unclear, "145 w"?).
Line numbers count from top of image-003.

003 L14 ... cũ? a . ꝯ? ꝑ ... ꝯ ... [illegible] ... p(ri)ma? . ꝯ . ꝯ(?)uersio? / diffinitio? 
003 L15 ꝑ ... a . q(uod)? ... ꝓ? ... f'? ... [illegible] ... a(liqu)a? . m? . i . n(on)? ... ꝯ
003 L16 ... ꝑ ... ꝓ ... [hole at lower left] ... ꝑ ... d(ic)im(us)? ... ꝑ ... (bottom, partly cut)
Honest assessment: again no continuous phrase secured. The only fairly confident word is "excellen-" (L5). The surface is abraded and stained; native resolution and contrast stretching did not raise legibility enough to read connected text.

FACE B LAYOUT (from overview image-004)
- image-004: reduced overview of the other face of the same strip (mirror shape: torn notch now at lower centre, pencil note now vertical at the LEFT edge, so this is the reverse).
- Two columns again, ~16 lines visible; brown staining over the upper half of the left column and the middle; text at lower right appears darker and better preserved. Several red paragraph marks at line starts in both columns (left col approx. lines 7, 9; mid-line ¶ at left col line 9; right col lines 2, 3, 6, 9 and mid-line). No large initial visible at this scale.
- Tiles image-005 (left) and image-006 (right) presumably cover it.

TILE image-005 (native tile, left part of face B: left column; at far right x>1300 the beginnings of right-column lines, overlapping image-006)
Viewed with crop rscratch/packet-17/005a.jpg (grey, autocontrast, 1.5x).
Pencil note at left edge, vertical: "Stams, StA, Fg. 145v" (so face A is presumably 145r).
Observations: the left column is the worst-preserved area of the packet: ink largely lost/abraded, brown stain across the top. Red paragraph marks at line 5 (left margin, x~130), line 9 (mid-line, x~520), line 11 (left margin), line 11 mid-line (x~900). ~14-15 lines visible.
Line numbers count from top of image-005.

005 L1-L3  [illegible: only scattered strokes under the stain]
005 L4  ... ꝯ ... [illegible] ... ꝗ? ... ſ̄ ... 
005 L5  [red ¶] [illegible] ... ꝓ ... ꝯ ... ꝗ? ... q(uod) ꝯ(tr)a? / ē(ss)e? ... 
005 L6  ... [illegible] ... ut p(ate)t? / ut p(ri)us? (x~920-1100, dark ink) ...
005 L7  ... ꝯ ... ꝗ ... ꝯ ... ꝓ? ... [illegible]
005 L8  ... ꝗ? ... ꝯ ... [illegible] ...
005 L9  ... [red ¶] [illegible] ... 
005 L10 ... n? . ꝯ? . ꝓ? ... [illegible]
005 L11 [red ¶] [illegible] ... [red ¶ mid-line] [illegible] ...
005 L12 ... ꝯ ... ꝓ ... [illegible] ...
005 L13 c? ... ꝯ ... [illegible] ... (bottom)
Right-column starts at x~1300-1557 (overlap with image-006; read there): L2 [red ¶] ..., L7 [red ¶] ..., L11 [red ¶] Si? quis? ..., L12 "si? hēat? ...".
Honest assessment: essentially unreadable on these images; nothing reliable beyond isolated abbreviations.

TILE image-006 (native tile, right part of face B: right column; left edge x<300 overlaps the right-column starts seen at the right edge of image-005)
Viewed with crops rscratch/packet-17/006a.jpg (upper) and 006b.jpg (lower), grey autocontrast 1.5x.
Observations: right column ~16 lines; best-preserved column of the packet but still abraded and creased. Red paragraph marks at line 3 (left margin x~250, i.e. the overlap zone), line 5 (mid-line, x~700), line 6 (mid-line, x~860), line 9 (left margin), line 12 (left margin), line 14 (mid-line, x~710). A green/grey stain at top centre. The right part of the tile is blank margin; no text cut at the right edge of the column.
Line numbers count from top of image-006.

006 L1  (cut at top) ... [illegible] ... ꝗ? ... ꝯ? ...
006 L2  ... ꝑ? ꝓ ... ꝗ ... [illegible]

006 L7  esse? / ēē? ... ꝑ . a . c . ... ꝗ? ... [illegible] ... ſ(ecundu)m? . b . ꝓ? ho(c)? mo(do)? / ꝓ hemo? (end of line; the letters "hemo" or "hō mō" are fairly clear but the expansion is not)
006 L8  D?(ic)? ig(itu)r? . ... a . ... [illegible] ... ꝗ̄? ... 
006 L9  [red ¶] [illegible] ... ꝯ? ... uis? a(utem)? ... aliq(ui)s? / aliquo? ... [illegible] ... ꝓ? b?

006 L12 [red ¶] Si quis? / Siq(ui)s? ꝑ(?) ... l? ꝗ ... ſ(ecundu)m? ... [illegible] ... ꝑ(?)
006 L13 si? hēat? (= habeat?) ... ꝯ? ... b? ... ꝓ ... ꝓ? ... ꝯ ... 
006 L14 [illegible] ... [red ¶ mid-line] [illegible] ... 
006 L15 [illegible] (bottom, cut)
Honest assessment: no continuous span of even three secure words. Tokens with some confidence: "a . c ." sigla (L6, L7), ". b ." (L7), red ¶ positions, "Si quis"/"Siq-" at L12 opening, "habeat"? at L13.

SUMMARY / LIMITATIONS
- Selected areas: I attempted every line of both columns on both faces (4 columns, ~15-17 lines each). None could be read as connected text; the brief's target of several 10-line spans was not achievable from these images. The leaf is abraded, stained (brown on face A right column and face B left column; green-grey on face B top) and creased; the hand is small and heavily abbreviated with many point-separated single letters (sigla such as a, b, c, d, g), suggesting a lettered argument (logical/mathematical/natural-philosophical style) -- this is an observation about form only.
- Most-confident tokens: face A right column L5 "excellen-" (twice?); face B right column L12 "Si quis"/"Siq-" after a red ¶; repeated ".a. .c." sigla.
- Pencil notes: face A right margin and face B left margin, "Stams, StA, Fg. 145" + r/v respectively (145v on face B is clear; face A suffix unclear).
- Suggestions: multispectral/UV imaging would be needed for a usable reading; a raking-light image of face A left column and face B left column might recover ink traces. Red/colour channels were not separately tested beyond greyscale autocontrast.
- I did not stop on the image limit.
